## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

For a sufficiently smooth solution, the time-step remainder is locally $O(\Delta t^2)$. Summing $N=T/\Delta t$ such errors over a fixed interval generally yields a global $O(\Delta t)$ bound only with the required consistency and stability estimates; one cannot discard every local term without controlling their accumulation.

Taking the step size to zero recovers the original differential equation, which may remain nonlinear. Superposition is instead a property of its first-variation equation around a common nominal motion. For example, the exact solution of $\dot x=x^2$ is $x(t)=a/(1-at)$ while it exists. Adding two initial values does not add those finite solutions. See [dynamics](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-2-dynamics.html) and [the explicit remainder example](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-4-residuals-curvature.html).

## Taylor Expansion

$$
x(t+\Delta t) = x(t) + f(x,u)\Delta t + O(\Delta t^2).
$$

## Limit Argument

As $\Delta t \to 0$, second-order terms vanish, preserving
exact linear accumulation of first-order variations.

:::
